pr_title: fix(rust, python): read_csv was parsing dates incorrectly when the dtype was overridden
pr_body:
closes #9102 

The main idea here is:
- instead of using `try_from(pattern)`, use `try_from_with_unit(pattern, unit)`

Then, instead of having to do
```rust
infer = try_from(pattern);
infer.transform = match time_unit {
    ...
}
```
you can just do
```rust
infer = try_from_with_unit(pattern, time_unit);
```

It also means you can pass the `time_unit` forwards within the `slow_datetime_parser`

To get the `time_unit`, it needs to be an argument of `parse_bytes`. I've made it of type `Option<TimeUnit>`, so that when parsing non-datetime type (e.g. Utf8), then `time_unit` can be set to `None`, and for `datetime`, it can either be the default `Microsecond` or whatever the user overrid it with
pr_comments: thanks for your review! ok shipping then

issue_context.title: Issues parsing nanosecond Datetimes
comments:
thanks @Michael-J-Ward for the report! Will take a look

Here's some simple python reproducers to make this easier to debug / test:

1) (agree that this is a bug)
```python
In [13]: data = """\
    ...: a,b
    ...: 2020-01-01T00:00:00.123456789,199
    ...: """

In [14]: pl.read_csv(io.StringIO(data), try_parse_dates=True, dtypes={'a': pl.Datetime('ns')})
Out[14]:
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────────────────────────────┬─────┐
│ a                             ┆ b   │
│ ---                           ┆ --- │
│ datetime[ns]                  ┆ i64 │
╞═══════════════════════════════╪═════╡
│ 1970-01-19 06:17:16.800123456 ┆ 199 │
└───────────────────────────────┴─────┘
```

2) (not sure about this one, maybe it just needs better docs, saying that auto-inference defaults to microseconds)
```python
In [15]: pl.read_csv(io.StringIO(data), try_parse_dates=True)
Out[15]:
shape: (1, 2)
┌────────────────────────────┬─────┐
│ a                          ┆ b   │
│ ---                        ┆ --- │
│ datetime[μs]               ┆ i64 │
╞════════════════════════════╪═════╡
│ 2020-01-01 00:00:00.123456 ┆ 199 │
└────────────────────────────┴─────┘
```

3) 
Is this right? You wrote
```rust
    let test1 = df.clone().lazy().with_column(
        col("start")
            .str()
            .strptime(dt_type_no_tz, strptime_options.clone())
            .alias("start_dt")
    ).collect().unwrap();
    println!("{:?}", test1);

    let expected = &dt_type_with_tz;
    let received = df.column("start_dt").unwrap().dtype();
    // fails because received has no timezone
    assert_eq!(expected, received); // comment this out to hit the 2nd assert
```
but I presume `received` should use `test1`, not `df`? Does the issue still reproduce if you change that?

> Are there other examples where polars defaults to silently truncating or otherwise discarding data?

Yup, `to_datetime` defaults to `'us'`, so that may also end up discarding data:
```
>>> pl.Series(['2020-01-01T00:00:00.123456789']).str.to_datetime()
shape: (1,)
Series: '' [datetime[μs]]
[
	2020-01-01 00:00:00.123456
]
```
But there, overwriting `'ns'` actually works:
```python
>>> pl.Series(['2020-01-01T00:00:00.123456789']).str.to_datetime(time_unit='ns')
shape: (1,)
Series: '' [datetime[ns]]
[
	2020-01-01 00:00:00.123456789
]
>>> 
```
So, I think all that needs doing here is to
1. fix the overwriting behaviour for `dtypes` in `read_csv`
2. document that `'us'` is the default for `try_parse_dates`

For your 3rd point - thanks, here's a simple Python reproducer:
```python
>>> pl.Series(['2020-01-01T00:00:00.123456789+00:00']).str.to_datetime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%.f%#z', time_unit='ns', exact=False)
shape: (1,)
Series: '' [datetime[ns]]
[
	2020-01-01 00:00:00.123456789
]
```

I'll take a look - thanks again for your excellent reports, this is how software gets better!

review_comments: just preserving the status-quo here, but perhaps this could also be more precise - will take a look
